title: The Girl Who Fixed Things
text:
Priya's mother called her a magpie, because she could not pass a discarded appliance without stopping. Broken fans, cracked radios, a rice cooker somebody had abandoned by the lift lobby — all of them found their way onto the small workbench on her balcony.
Most of her repairs failed. Screws rolled under the sofa and vanished. Wires that looked identical turned out to matter enormously. Twice she gave herself a small electric shock and decided, briefly, to take up a safer hobby.
But the fan she mended in September ran all through the year, and when the neighbour's kettle died, it was Priya's door they knocked on. She had learned something her classmates had not: that being clever is mostly the habit of trying one more time after the last attempt has failed.
